target: IEEE Open Journal of the Computer Society
purpose: Integrate Codex Papers 1 and 2; distinguish estimation accuracy, uncertainty construction and measurement validity in bounded annotation audits.
approval_source: User approved the OJCS revision and two targeted experiments; paid resource amount must be concrete before provisioning.
prior_exposure: All retained synthetic, nuImages and Paper 1 results are development evidence. New seeds do not make known generator families unseen. The current review has used no protected human record.
claims_allowed_before_new_results: The retained joint 10 percent improvement target failed.
Existing comparisons are implementation-specific, not a general impossibility result for prediction assistance.
Paper 1 contains one-rater operational judgments, not independently verified physical omissions.

contribution_gate.decision: GO for the bounded empirical revision, not submission GO
contribution_gate.reason: The published RLFA framework already supplies prediction-assisted without-replacement inference. The useful remaining question is whether the historical accuracy-width gap persists when the uncertainty construction changes on the same observations and forecasts, and how that result transfers to another known-deletion frame.
contribution_gate.no_claim: No new general estimator, no broad state of the art result, no guaranteed journal acceptance.

experiment_1.question: Does changing the interval construction resolve the historical weak width improvement at the same measured-image budget?
experiment_1.unit: One independently generated finite population and one paired sampling order per replicate; no reuse of a population counted as an independent population.
new_strong_intervals: Qualified RLFA with identical past-only forecasts
experiment_1.anchors: Retained 13 point methods and their interval implementations, with source departures and guarantee classes disclosed.
experiment_1.isolation: RLFA past-only and retained sequential interval receive the same measurement order and forecasts; the point estimate is unchanged. RLFA fixed is paired to the raw-proxy setting. ConBo uses no predictor. Other sampling designs retain their own honest budgets and are not described as identical sample sets.
experiment_1.optimization: Exact rational backend, permanent running rejection pruning and certified monotone endpoint search; no scientific tuning. Reference agreement required before use.
experiment_1.closed_branch: Do not expand the failed integer point-band utility study. Its existing negative result is retained in the supplement.

experiment_2.question: Does the pattern transfer from synthetic populations and nuImages to a fixed additional real-image known-deletion frame?
experiment_2.dataset: COCO val2017; 1000 images selected solely by hash of official image IDs before inspecting object outcomes
experiment_2.model: torchvision Faster R-CNN ResNet50 FPN V2, COCO_V1 weights, one frozen checkpoint; no training or model selection
experiment_2.model_exposure: COCO-trained detector; validation benchmark may have informed provider model development. This is a transfer study of the audit procedure, not independent detector generalization or natural-omission validation.
experiment_2.target: Deleted non-crowd provider person instances with positive in-image boxes and height at least 25 pixels. At most 20 eligible targets per image, chosen by a fixed annotation-ID hash when necessary. All non-target annotations remain available for matching. The target is the capped constructed count, not every physical person.
experiment_2.image_selection: Take the first 1000 official val2017 image IDs after sorting SHA256(namespace|image_id). No replacements based on annotations, detector performance or experimental outcomes. Missing or corrupt files stop execution.
experiment_2.deletion_rule: SHA256-derived uniforms keyed by fixed namespace, scenario and annotation ID; fixed once before audit randomization.
experiment_2.predictor: Person detections at score >=0.5; original-image height >=25; maximum-cardinality then maximum-IoU one-to-one matching at IoU >=0.5 to retained eligible person annotations. Six count/height features plus three full-frame leave-one-out count features; COCO has no invented drive groups.
experiment_2.scope: Same methods, cap and budgets as Experiment 1; 1000 independent audit orders for each of three fixed deletion frames; repetitions are not independent datasets.
experiment_2.licenses: COCO annotation CC BY 4.0; images retain their individual Flickr rights. Release code, IDs, derived counts and provenance, not a new image archive.

endpoints: MSE and mean conditional-risk score where justified
Mean interval width and full logical-support frequency
Coverage of the constructed total; running-set coverage for the strong confidence sequences
Runtime and measured-image budget including all predictor fitting labels
analysis.primary_interval_contrast: Paired mean width difference: RLFA past-only minus historical sequential interval, separately for each of M01-M06 at b=200.
analysis.primary_effect_size: Mean width ratio and paired difference; no outcome-dependent redefinition of success.
analysis.uncertainty: Report paired Monte Carlo standard errors and 95 percent t intervals as approximate simulation uncertainty; also provide bounded empirical-Bernstein simultaneous intervals for six primary width differences. Do not relabel an inconclusive finite-sample contrast as established superiority.
analysis.coverage: Report exact binomial intervals for independent simulations; Holm-adjusted one-sided tests for coverage below 95 percent across the predeclared new cells. An observed 95 percent estimate is not proof of the nominal guarantee.
analysis.sample_size_reason: 1000 independent repetitions give approximately 0.69 percentage points standard error at 95 percent coverage (about 1.35 points for an unadjusted normal 95 percent half-width); exact intervals will be used. This is a precision target, not a power guarantee for every width contrast.
analysis.failures: Keep every planned replicate. Empty sets count as noncoverage and receive full logical-support width in utility scoring, while also being reported separately. Numerical errors halt the run and remain in the ledger; no silent seed replacement.
analysis.old_target: The old joint 10 percent MSE-and-width target against both direct and stratified auditing remains NOT_ATTAINED; no new result retroactively changes it.

execution_limits.research_branching: No additional algorithms, datasets, predictors, hyperparameter sweeps or extra repetitions in response to unfavorable findings.
execution_limits.engineering_limit: Two bounded implementation changes for runtime: exact GMP rationals and exact running/end-point evaluation. Both already implemented; further optimization requires a concrete blocker review.
execution_limits.cloud: One task-owned compute resource at a time; no new persistent S3/network volumes unless strictly necessary and separately itemized. No use or mutation of Claude-owned resources.
execution_limits.spending: No resource is provisioned until a live rate, full-job estimate and user-approved ceiling exist.
execution_limits.stop: Hard process deadlines, checkpointed outputs, automatic compute shutdown plus independent controller; verify terminal provider state; remove task-created disks after verified local evidence transfer.
execution_limits.scope_change: Pause for a concrete decision if evidence requires expanded scientific scope, unavailable access, an increased spending ceiling or more than the planned active-work allowance.
